interface.title: SpectraGuard - SERS Spectrum Quality Analyzer
interface.field: Vibrational spectroscopy (Raman / SERS / IR), analytical chemistry
interface.stage_of_work: Data quality control after acquisition and before analysis or inclusion in a dataset
interface.what_it_is_for: Score how trustworthy a single Raman/SERS spectrum is: an overall 0-100 Confidence Score with a grade, six per-metric scores, a radar overview, a spectrum-vs-baseline plot and a downloadable text report.
interface.gap_between_readme_and_app: The README says each score comes with an uncertainty (bootstrap confidence interval, ± value, grade stability). This web app shows no uncertainty anywhere, neither in the UI nor in the TXT report, and the reviewer found no uncertainty code in app.py.
interface.outside_this_interface: The README's modality choice (SERS / Raman / IR), batch QC of many spectra and streaming QC exist only in the command-line tool and API. This Streamlit page scores one spectrum at a time and has no modality selector.

data.note: Mostly the built-in demo spectra (Good/Marginal/Bad, 1500 points, 200-3200 cm⁻¹). The uploaded test file good_spectrum.csv (36 points, 400-1800 cm⁻¹) loaded but scored 22.5 'Poor', with 0 peaks detected, although three clear peaks show in the plot. The uploaded test file poor_spectrum.csv (37 points loaded) made the app crash with 'ValueError: array must not contain infs or NaNs' in calculate_snr/savgol_filter, so the malformed row was not skipped. Demo scores: Good 67.7 'Good', Marginal 53.5 'Marginal', Bad 43.3 'Marginal' (the Bad preset is not graded Poor). Hotspot Uniformity was 0.000 in every case. Baseline Stability scored higher for Marginal (0.739) and Bad (0.757) than for Good (0.649). No uncertainty is shown next to any score, although the README promises one (see interface.gap_between_readme_and_app). The replay's screen IDs in check.json refer to the replay's own folder check/screens/, not to the explorer's screens/ folder.

screens_never_reached: A scored result for poor_spectrum.csv: the upload crashed with 'ValueError: array must not contain infs or NaNs' (screens/019.webp), so no score, metrics or report could be produced
Avg FWHM in Diagnostics for the uploaded good_spectrum.csv: it was not shown because 0 peaks were detected (screens/018.webp)
not_done: Could not compare the uploaded good and poor files: adding poor_spectrum.csv with the uploader's + button crashed scoring with a ValueError traceback (screens/019.webp). Its malformed row is turned into NaN rather than skipped as the code notes expected.

The uploaded good_spectrum.csv did not score well as the notes expected. It got 22.5 'Poor' with SNR 0.023, 0 peaks detected and Raw SNR 1.1, likely because 36 coarse points are too few for the smoothing and peak-finding steps. So the goal of uploading a measured spectrum and judging it fairly only partly worked.
The README says each score should be read with its uncertainty, but no uncertainty or confidence interval is shown anywhere in the UI or the report.
Hotspot Uniformity was 0.000 for every spectrum. It seems to need multiple spectra or a map, and there is no control to supply one.
The 'Bad' demo is graded 'Marginal' (43.3), not 'Poor', so the presets do not produce three distinct grades.

Could not restore the hidden Spectrum trace by clicking its legend entry again (screens/025.webp); the chart only came back after switching the demo preset. The replay found legend clicks apply after a short delay, so this may be a timing issue rather than a broken toggle.
No TXT/TSV test file was available, so only the CSV upload path was tried.
The app has no explicit keep/re-measure recommendation. That decision has to be made by the user from the grade and metrics (task n1).
